newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian government condemns paramilitary groups.
newsitem.headline: Colombian government condemns paramilitary groups.

text.p: A top official on Thursday condemned right-wing paramilitary groups operating across Colombia, saying they were as responsible as leftist rebels for seemingly uncontrolled violence.
"This is criminal behaviour," Interior Minister Horacio Serpa said of the groups, which have grabbed recent headlines by kidnapping family members of prominent guerrilla leaders.
"They are fostering violence, just as guerrillas do, and causing a lot of harm and violence in our country."

Serpa's remarks to reporters came after he held talks with the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Colombia to discuss the fate of 60 soldiers taken prisoner on Aug. 30 when the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) overran a military base in southwestern Putumayo province.

He said there was no word on when the soldiers might be freed but he warned that the kidnapping of guerrilla leaders' family members threatened to "radicalize the dirty war" between gunmen of the left and right in Colombia and "unleash a diabolical chain of retaliations."

A right-wing group known as the Self-Defence Committee of Uraba and Cordoba has claimed responsibilty for kidnapping at least five family members of top guerrilla commanders over the past two months. Rebel leaders have condemned the abductions and accused the military of carrying them out with the tacit support of the government.
